visit_presentations.presentation:
A 30-year-old G3P2 participant presented for routine study screening on Apr 15, 2026 at 34 weeks and 4 days of gestation. Her medical-history assessment recorded no previous medical conditions, surgery or allergies. Prior or concomitant medication use during the preceding 30 days was reported. Her obstetric history included 2 previous live births and 2 prior vaginal deliveries. Previous pregnancy complications included raised blood pressure. A family history of hypertension was documented.

Blood pressure was 115/76 mmHg, remained 110/70 mmHg on repeat measurement, heart rate was 80 bpm, respiratory rate was 14 breaths/min, oxygen saturation was 97%, temporal temperature was 35.8°C and weight was 64 kg. Urine protein dipstick was trace.

The dating ultrasound was performed on Jan 05, 2026 at 20 weeks and 2 days, with an expected delivery date of May 23, 2026. The scan recorded an estimated fetal weight of 348 g and cephalic presentation presentation. Fetal movement, amniotic-fluid volume and placental position were recorded as normal.

Laboratory results are presented in the table below.

On Apr 22, 2026, at 34 weeks and 1 day of gestation, the participant attended the scheduled Visit 2 antenatal follow-up. Her health status was recorded as unchanged, with the description “Stable.” Pulmonary oedema was not recorded.

Blood pressure was 113/78 mmHg. Heart rate was 112 bpm, respiratory rate was 19 breaths/min, oxygen saturation was 98%, temporal temperature was 36.1°C and weight was 65 kg. Urine protein dipstick was negative.

No medication changes were reported. No new adverse events or changes to existing adverse events were reported.

No obstetric ultrasound was documented for this visit.

Laboratory results and their source-recorded interpretations are presented in the table below.

On Apr 29, 2026, at 36 weeks and 5 days of gestation, the participant attended the scheduled Visit 3 antenatal follow-up. Her health status was recorded as unchanged, with the description “NORMAL.” Pulmonary oedema was not recorded.

Blood pressure was initially 108/58 mmHg, with a second recorded measurement of 106/67 mmHg; the interval between measurements was unavailable. Heart rate was 81 bpm, respiratory rate was 17 breaths/min, oxygen saturation was 96%, temporal temperature was 35.9°C and weight was 66 kg. Urine protein dipstick was negative.

No medication changes were reported. No new adverse events or changes to existing adverse events were reported.

No obstetric ultrasound was documented for this visit.

Laboratory results and their source-recorded interpretations are presented in the table below.
Visit 4 was not performed. The source-recorded reason was “Delivered.” No clinical assessment is attributed to Visit 4. Delivery is documented on May 14, 2026 and is presented under Visit 5.

Vaginal delivery occurred on May 13, 2026 at 38 weeks and 4 days of gestation. The delivery outcome assessment was completed on May 14, 2026. No complication at delivery was recorded.

Estimated maternal blood loss was 150 mL. No blood transfusion was recorded. No postpartum infection was recorded. Postpartum health status was recorded as normal. The participant remained in hospital for 2 days. She was not readmitted. Her subsequent health status was recorded as improved, with the description “WELL AND RECOVERING.”

A liveborn female infant was recorded with a birth weight of 2,860 g, length 49 cm and head circumference 36 cm. Apgar scores were 8, 9 and 9 at 1, 5 and 10 minutes, respectively. The recorded neonatal heart rate was 135 bpm and respiratory rate was 32 breaths/min. No neonatal intensive-care admission, respiratory distress syndrome, intraventricular haemorrhage, congenital anomaly or birth complication was recorded.

On Jun 10, 2026, 28 days after the documented delivery on May 13, 2026, the participant attended the final postpartum follow-up. Her final health status was recorded as improved, with the description “STABLE.” Pulmonary oedema was not recorded.

Blood pressure was initially 128/91 mmHg, with a second recorded measurement of 129/85 mmHg; the interval between measurements was unavailable. Heart rate was 98 bpm, respiratory rate was 15 breaths/min, oxygen saturation was 96%, temporal temperature was 36.2°C and weight was 60 kg. Urine protein dipstick was negative. No maternal hospitalization or intensive-care admission was recorded.

No medication changes were reported. No new adverse events or changes to existing adverse events were reported.

The infant assessment recorded a female infant with a birth weight of 2,860 g, length 50 cm and head circumference 34 cm. Apgar scores were 8, 9 and 10 at 1, 5 and 10 minutes, respectively. The recorded neonatal heart rate was 136 bpm and respiratory rate was 32 breaths/min. No neonatal intensive-care admission, respiratory distress syndrome, intraventricular haemorrhage, congenital anomaly or birth complication was recorded.

Laboratory results and their source-recorded interpretations are presented in the table below.

cases.overall_presentation:
A 30-year-old G3P2 participant entered the study on Apr 15, 2026 at 34 weeks and 4 days of gestation. Her previous pregnancy history included raised blood pressure. Gestational dating was based on the ultrasound performed on Jan 05, 2026 at 20 weeks and 2 days. At screening, blood pressure was 115/76 mmHg, the repeat was 110/70 mmHg and urine protein was trace.

No antenatal blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg or higher was recorded. Urine protein changed from trace to negative across the available antenatal assessments.

Vaginal delivery occurred on May 13, 2026 at 38 weeks and 4 days. No delivery complication was recorded. Maternal outcome records show estimated maternal blood loss was 150 mL, no transfusion was recorded, no postpartum infection was recorded and the hospital stay was 2 days. A liveborn female infant was recorded with a birth weight of 2,860 g. Apgar scores were 8 at 1 minute, 9 at 5 minutes and 9 at 10 minutes.

At postpartum follow-up on Jun 10, 2026, blood pressure was 128/91 mmHg, 129/85 mmHg on repeat and urine protein was negative. Her health status was recorded as improved, with the description “STABLE.” No maternal hospitalization or intensive-care admission was recorded.

Unresolved source issue: the canonical age of 30 years conflicts with source-recorded age 29 years.

visit_presentations.presentation:
A 41-year-old G4P2 participant presented for routine study screening on May 12, 2026 at 30 weeks and 3 days of gestation. Her medical history included Hypertension and Diabetes Type II. Prior or concomitant medication use during the preceding 30 days was reported. Her obstetric history included 2 previous live births, one miscarriage and 2 prior caesarean sections. The recorded caesarean indication included other and macrosomic baby, hypertension. Previous pregnancy complications included raised blood pressure. A family history of hypertension was documented.

Blood pressure was 114/78 mmHg, remained 118/76 mmHg on repeat measurement, heart rate was 90 bpm, respiratory rate was 15 breaths/min, oxygen saturation was 96%, temporal temperature was 36.6°C and weight was 82.8 kg. Urine protein dipstick was negative.

The dating ultrasound was performed on Jan 27, 2026 at 15 weeks and 3 days, with an expected delivery date of Jul 18, 2026. The scan recorded an estimated fetal weight of 120 g, cephalic presentation and a fetal heart rate of 159 bpm. Fetal movement, amniotic-fluid volume and placental position were recorded as normal. Cervical length was 4.3 cm.

Laboratory results are presented in the table below.

On May 21, 2026, at 31 weeks and 5 days of gestation, the participant attended the scheduled Visit 2 antenatal follow-up. Her health status was recorded as unchanged, with the description “Clinically stable.” Pulmonary oedema was not recorded.

Blood pressure was initially 128/85 mmHg, with a second recorded measurement of 127/86 mmHg; the interval between measurements was unavailable. Heart rate was 78 bpm, respiratory rate was 14 breaths/min, oxygen saturation was 95%, temporal temperature was 36.7°C and weight was 83 kg. Urine protein dipstick was negative.

No medication changes were reported. No new adverse events or changes to existing adverse events were reported.

An obstetric ultrasound was performed on May 19, 2026. Fetal heart rate was 140 bpm. Fetal movement and placental position were recorded as normal. Estimated fetal weight was not documented. Ultrasound presentation was marked as available, but the presentation description was unavailable.

Laboratory results and their source-recorded interpretations are presented in the table below.

On May 27, 2026, at 32 weeks and 4 days of gestation, the participant attended the scheduled Visit 3 antenatal follow-up. Her health status was recorded as unchanged, with the description “CLINICALLY STABLE.” Pulmonary oedema was not recorded.

Blood pressure was initially 132/89 mmHg, with a second recorded measurement of 129/88 mmHg; the interval between measurements was unavailable. Heart rate was 82 bpm, respiratory rate was 16 breaths/min, oxygen saturation was 94%, temporal temperature was 36.6°C and weight was 83 kg. Urine protein dipstick was trace.

No medication changes were reported. No new adverse events or changes to existing adverse events were reported.

No obstetric ultrasound was documented for this visit.

Laboratory results and their source-recorded interpretations are presented in the table below.

On Jun 11, 2026, at 34 weeks and 5 days of gestation, the participant attended the scheduled Visit 4 antenatal follow-up. Her health status was recorded as unchanged, with the description “clinically stable.” Pulmonary oedema was not recorded.

Blood pressure was initially 129/78 mmHg, with a second recorded measurement of 125/75 mmHg; the interval between measurements was unavailable. Heart rate was 90 bpm, respiratory rate was 18 breaths/min, oxygen saturation was 98%, temporal temperature was 36.4°C and weight was 82 kg. Urine protein dipstick was negative.

No medication changes were reported. No new adverse events or changes to existing adverse events were reported.

No obstetric ultrasound was documented for this visit.

Laboratory results and their source-recorded interpretations are presented in the table below.

Caesarean delivery occurred on Jun 29, 2026 at 37 weeks and 2 days of gestation. The recorded indication was two previous caesarean sections. No complication at delivery was recorded.

Estimated maternal blood loss was 200 mL. No blood transfusion was recorded. No postpartum infection was recorded. Postpartum health status was recorded as normal. The participant remained in hospital for 2 days. She was not readmitted. Her subsequent health status was recorded as unchanged, with the description “Clinically stable.”

A liveborn male infant was recorded with a birth weight of 2,550 g, length 45 cm and head circumference 36 cm. Apgar scores were 8 and 9 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The recorded neonatal heart rate was 145 bpm and respiratory rate was 41 breaths/min. No neonatal intensive-care admission, congenital anomaly or birth complication was recorded.

The delivery form recorded gestational age as 37 weeks and 3 days, while the approved dating calculation gives 37 weeks and 2 days. This conflicting source value requires verification.

On Jul 28, 2026, 29 days after the documented delivery on Jun 29, 2026, the participant attended the final postpartum follow-up. Her final health status was recorded as improved, with the description “CLINICALLY STABLE.” Pulmonary oedema was not recorded.

Blood pressure was initially 138/88 mmHg, with a second recorded measurement of 136/89 mmHg; the interval between measurements was unavailable. Heart rate was 88 bpm, respiratory rate was 18 breaths/min, oxygen saturation was 96%, temporal temperature was 36.2°C and weight was 77 kg. Urine protein dipstick was negative. No maternal hospitalization or intensive-care admission was recorded.

Medication changes were reported, but the medication details were unavailable in the supplied visit record. No new adverse events or changes to existing adverse events were reported.

The infant assessment recorded a male infant with a birth weight of 2,550 g, length 45 cm and head circumference 36 cm. Apgar scores were 8 and 9 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The recorded neonatal heart rate was 145 bpm and respiratory rate was 41 breaths/min. No neonatal intensive-care admission, respiratory distress syndrome, intraventricular haemorrhage, congenital anomaly or birth complication was recorded.

Laboratory results and their source-recorded interpretations are presented in the table below.

cases.overall_presentation:
A 41-year-old G4P2 participant entered the study on May 12, 2026 at 30 weeks and 3 days of gestation. Her previous pregnancy history included raised blood pressure. Gestational dating was based on the ultrasound performed on Jan 27, 2026 at 15 weeks and 3 days. At screening, blood pressure was 114/78 mmHg, the repeat was 118/76 mmHg and urine protein was negative.

No antenatal blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg or higher was recorded. Urine protein changed from negative to trace and negative across the available antenatal assessments.

Caesarean delivery occurred on Jun 29, 2026 at 37 weeks and 2 days. No delivery complication was recorded. Maternal outcome records show estimated maternal blood loss was 200 mL, no transfusion was recorded, no postpartum infection was recorded and the hospital stay was 2 days. A liveborn male infant was recorded with a birth weight of 2,550 g. Apgar scores were 8 at 1 minute and 9 at 5 minutes.

At postpartum follow-up on Jul 28, 2026, blood pressure was 138/88 mmHg, 136/89 mmHg on repeat and urine protein was negative. Her health status was recorded as improved, with the description “CLINICALLY STABLE.” No maternal hospitalization or intensive-care admission was recorded.

Unresolved source issues: the canonical age of 41 years conflicts with source-recorded age 40 years, Visit 2 marks fetal presentation as assessed or available without supplying the result and the delivery form GA of 37 weeks and 3 days conflicts with the approved dating calculation of 37 weeks and 2 days.

visit_presentations.presentation:
A 33-year-old G3P2 participant presented for routine study screening on May 27, 2026 at 34 weeks and 1 day of gestation. Her medical-history assessment recorded no previous medical conditions, surgery or allergies and no use of prior or concomitant medication during the preceding 30 days. Her obstetric history included 2 previous live births and 2 prior vaginal deliveries. No previous pregnancy complicated by raised blood pressure, pre-eclampsia, severe pre-eclampsia, eclampsia, HELLP syndrome and fetal growth restriction was recorded.

Blood pressure was 127/80 mmHg, remained 124/74 mmHg on repeat measurement, heart rate was 103 bpm, respiratory rate was 18 breaths/min, oxygen saturation was 93%, temporal temperature was 36.6°C and weight was 73 kg. Urine protein dipstick was negative.

The dating ultrasound was performed on Feb 13, 2026 at 19 weeks and 3 days, with an expected delivery date of Jul 07, 2026. The scan recorded an estimated fetal weight of 323 g, cephalic presentation and a fetal heart rate of 143 bpm. Fetal movement, amniotic-fluid volume and placental position were recorded as normal.

Laboratory results are presented in the table below.

On Jun 03, 2026, at 35 weeks and 1 day of gestation, the participant attended the scheduled Visit 2 antenatal follow-up. Her health status was recorded as unchanged, with the description “Clinically stable.” Pulmonary oedema was not recorded.

Blood pressure was initially 125/81 mmHg, with a second recorded measurement of 122/76 mmHg; the interval between measurements was unavailable. Heart rate was 100 bpm, respiratory rate was 18 breaths/min, oxygen saturation was 93%, temporal temperature was 36.8°C and weight was 73 kg. Urine protein dipstick was negative.

No medication changes were reported. No new adverse events or changes to existing adverse events were reported.

No obstetric ultrasound was documented for this visit.

Laboratory results and their source-recorded interpretations are presented in the table below.

On Jun 10, 2026, at 36 weeks and 1 day of gestation, the participant attended the scheduled Visit 3 antenatal follow-up. Her health status was recorded as unchanged, with the description “Clinically stable.” Pulmonary oedema was not recorded.

Blood pressure was 120/70 mmHg. An additional systolic measurement of 115 mmHg was recorded without a corresponding diastolic measurement. Heart rate was 90 bpm, respiratory rate was 18 breaths/min, oxygen saturation was 98%, temporal temperature was 36.1°C and weight was 74 kg. Urine protein dipstick was negative.

No medication changes were reported. No new adverse events or changes to existing adverse events were reported.

No obstetric ultrasound was documented for this visit.

Laboratory results and their source-recorded interpretations are presented in the table below.

On Jun 24, 2026, at 38 weeks and 1 day of gestation, the participant attended the scheduled Visit 4 antenatal follow-up. Her health status was recorded as improved, with the description “CLINICALLY STABLE.” Pulmonary oedema was not recorded.

Blood pressure was initially 114/69 mmHg, with a second recorded measurement of 115/72 mmHg; the interval between measurements was unavailable. Heart rate was 95 bpm, respiratory rate was 18 breaths/min, oxygen saturation was 95%, temporal temperature was 36.3°C and weight was 74 kg. Urine protein dipstick was negative.

No medication changes were reported. No new adverse events or changes to existing adverse events were reported.

No obstetric ultrasound was documented for this visit.

Laboratory results and their source-recorded interpretations are presented in the table below.

Vaginal delivery occurred on Jun 28, 2026 at 38 weeks and 5 days of gestation. The delivery outcome assessment was completed on Jun 29, 2026. No complication at delivery was recorded.

Estimated maternal blood loss was 800 mL. No blood transfusion was recorded. No postpartum infection was recorded. Postpartum health status was recorded as normal. The participant remained in hospital for 2 days. She was not readmitted. Her subsequent health status was recorded as unchanged, with the description “Clinically stable.”

A liveborn female infant was recorded with a birth weight of 3,200 g, length 50 cm and head circumference 35 cm. Apgar scores were 9, 9 and 9 at 1, 5 and 10 minutes, respectively. The recorded neonatal heart rate was 137 bpm and respiratory rate was 37 breaths/min. No neonatal intensive-care admission, congenital anomaly or birth complication was recorded.

On Jul 28, 2026, 30 days after the documented delivery on Jun 28, 2026, the participant attended the final postpartum follow-up. Her final health status was recorded as unchanged, with the description “CLINICALLY STABLE.” Pulmonary oedema was not recorded.

Blood pressure was initially 129/85 mmHg, with a second recorded measurement of 127/84 mmHg; the interval between measurements was unavailable. Heart rate was 88 bpm, respiratory rate was 18 breaths/min, oxygen saturation was 96%, temporal temperature was 36.6°C and weight was 67 kg. Urine protein dipstick was negative. No maternal hospitalization or intensive-care admission was recorded.

No medication changes were reported. No new adverse events or changes to existing adverse events were reported.

The infant assessment recorded a female infant with a birth weight of 3,200 g, length 50 cm and head circumference 35 cm. Apgar scores were 9, 9 and 9 at 1, 5 and 10 minutes, respectively. The recorded neonatal heart rate was 137 bpm and respiratory rate was 37 breaths/min. No neonatal intensive-care admission, respiratory distress syndrome, intraventricular haemorrhage, congenital anomaly or birth complication was recorded.

cases.overall_presentation:
A 33-year-old G3P2 participant entered the study on May 27, 2026 at 34 weeks and 1 day of gestation. No previous hypertensive pregnancy complication was recorded. Gestational dating was based on the ultrasound performed on Feb 13, 2026 at 19 weeks and 3 days. At screening, blood pressure was 127/80 mmHg, the repeat was 124/74 mmHg and urine protein was negative.

No antenatal blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg or higher was recorded. Urine protein was negative when assessed.

Vaginal delivery occurred on Jun 28, 2026 at 38 weeks and 5 days. No delivery complication was recorded. Maternal outcome records show estimated maternal blood loss was 800 mL, no transfusion was recorded, no postpartum infection was recorded and the hospital stay was 2 days. A liveborn female infant was recorded with a birth weight of 3,200 g. Apgar scores were 9 at 1 minute, 9 at 5 minutes and 9 at 10 minutes.

At postpartum follow-up on Jul 28, 2026, blood pressure was 129/85 mmHg, 127/84 mmHg on repeat and urine protein was negative. Her health status was recorded as unchanged, with the description “CLINICALLY STABLE.” No maternal hospitalization or intensive-care admission was recorded.
